title: [ORION-QG QG-13 V3] Three-column combined-edit theorem mining for R6I support-five tightness
body:
Parent theorem-miner: #767
V2 obstruction owner: #777 / PR #779
Tightness owner: #762
Frozen base: `cad8b1b4d3be3668449658d10ef718eb1682d1c9`
Branch: `shadow/orion-qg-qg13-v3-r6i-three-column-edits`

## Status

**PROSPECTIVE SUCCESSOR PACKET — V2 remains immutable.**

QG-13 V2 proved that the frozen two-column E2 grammar is insufficient: among 216 support-five QG-1-irreducible structural patterns, 132 are covered by globally safe syndrome-cancelling two-column edits and 84 remain uncovered. The first canonical obstruction is committed under #777.

V3 changes exactly one scientific degree of freedom: edit arity increases from two distinct columns to **three distinct columns**. The local action alphabet and semantics remain unchanged.

## Frozen local actions

Per selected column:
- `A`: zero R0, recompute dependent R2;
- `B`: zero R1, recompute R2;
- `AB`: zero both independent generators, R2=I.

No Tag repair; targets, Tag, permutation, central choice and other block unchanged.

## Three-column safety rule

For action/signature classes synthesized from the complete local R6I resource table, a triple `(a,b,c)` may be used only if:

1. the XOR of its three inferred five-bit syndrome changes is zero;
2. the sum of the three exact per-class worst local cost deltas is <=0;
3. the action deletes at least one generator letter on each selected column;
4. applying it to a structural pattern strictly lowers `(max_generator_support,total_generator_support)`.

Because the R6I objective has no cross-column Restore factor, the sum of exact per-class maxima is a valid exact worst-case bound for independently chosen columns.

## Frozen global domain

Recompute from production semantics the same canonical five-column structural domain used by V2:
- accepting total five-bit block syndrome;
- QG-1 SOLO/PAIR irreducible;
- at least one generator support exactly five.

V3 may not narrow to only the 84 V2 rows during theorem scoring; it must report coverage over the full frozen support-five domain and separately report whether all 84 V2-uncovered patterns are now covered.

## Honest outcomes

- `QG13V3_SUPPORT4_CANDIDATE`: every support-five irreducible pattern has a globally safe three-column move. Still candidate-only; all-n theorem authority remains false.
- `QG13V3_V2_OBSTRUCTIONS_CLOSED_BUT_NEW_OBSTRUCTION_REMAINS`: all 84 V2 obstructions are closed but another support-five pattern remains under V3 scoring.
- `QG13V3_MINIMAL_THREE_COLUMN_OBSTRUCTION`: at least one V2 obstruction survives all globally safe three-column edits; serialize the first.
- `QG13V3_RESOURCE_BOUNDARY`: no globally safe three-column class exists.
- semantic/binding/CANNOT_CHECK terminals remain fail-closed.

## Anti-leakage

- V3 code starts from current main, not the V2 branch.
- V2 committed result may be opened only after V3 synthesizes its own action triples and structural census; it is then used solely to score closure of the 84 prior obstruction patterns.
- no chemistry/protected subject; no network;
- no post-outcome action or arity widening.

## Claim boundary

A V3 candidate does not prove support<=4 for all n until #762 opens a separate all-n theorem packet. Generic CEGIS/rewrite synthesis/finite-field dependence remain donor-owned.
